comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA bachelor curriculum for a Fall 2026 entrant, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official full-time curriculum supplies an exact 60+60+60=180 EC pathway. Year 1 is a shared 60-EC foundation in Dutch studies, literature, literacy, public debate and writing. Year 2 has 36 EC compulsory work, 12 EC restricted choice and 12 EC open choice. Year 3 has 30 EC open choice, one coherent 12-EC restricted-choice pair and an 18-EC bachelor project. The first two listed year-2 choices and the first-listed coherent year-3 Linguistics pair are selected neutrally; open choice remains uninstantiated.

routeSelection.basis: The generic normalized target names no specialization. The curriculum offers four coherent 12-EC year-3 restricted-choice pairs and no pair is established as more general; the first-listed Linguistics pair is selected independently of UCR fit. For the separate year-2 two-of-four choice, the first two listed options are selected by the same neutral rule.

core: Dutch language, linguistics, variation and historical development
Dutch literature, storytelling, interpretation and literary culture
Writing, rhetoric, argumentation and public communication
Dutch cultural history, contemporary society and independent humanities research
questions: How do language structures and variation shape Dutch communication and identity?
How do literary texts and stories create meaning within culture and society?
How can research, argumentation and writing address public and professional questions?

alternatives.label: Language, literature & public communication
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines literary and media analysis, rhetoric, writing, cultural history and public communication as the closest feasible UCR response to the integrated Dutch-language programme.
alternatives.concept: An integrated response to Dutch Language and Culture through literary study, narrative and film, rhetoric, writing, media, cultural history, philosophy and qualitative research, while acknowledging that UCR does not provide Dutch linguistics or a Dutch-language disciplinary sequence.
progression: Introductions to literature, film, rhetoric, archaeology, history and philosophy precede documentary, adaptation, environmental media, advanced film-and-text work, persuasive communication and creative communication. Formal prerequisites and verified offerings are respected; seven courses are level 3.

alternatives.label: Literature, writing & cultural history
alternatives.labelReason: This route concentrates on literary interpretation, creative and critical writing, historical context, visual culture, heritage and cultural research.
alternatives.concept: Develops the target’s literature, storytelling and Dutch cultural-history evidence through literary studies, media, art history, heritage, sociology, philosophy, creative communication and independent historical research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, six courses replace rhetoric, archaeology, environmental media and philosophy with Western art history, Renaissance culture, social theory and a history research seminar. The resulting programme gives more weight to cultural history, heritage and visual-literary interpretation.
progression: Foundations in literature, film, art history, history and sociology precede documentary, literary travel writing, museums, media and race, advanced literary meaning, creative communication and independent historical research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings are respected; eight courses are level 3.

alternatives.label: Language, public debate & society
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum foregrounds rhetoric, communication, audiences, identity, social research and institutions as a distinct response to language in public life.
alternatives.concept: Develops language-in-society, debate and contemporary cultural analysis through rhetoric, communication, literature, media, sociology, audience research, philosophy, leadership and public-facing research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, ten courses replace archaeological, literary and visual-cultural depth with social research, contemporary sociology, organisational leadership, market research and public communication. Twelve courses differ from the literature and cultural-history direction.
progression: Introductory media, rhetoric, sociology and research methods precede documentary and environmental media, audience research, social theory, persuasive and creative communication, organisational leadership, market research and philosophy. All prerequisites and verified offerings are respected; eight courses are level 3.

blocks: The Art of Rhetorical Communication supplies a foundation in language use and argument, without substituting for Dutch linguistics.
Style & Meaning provides close analysis of linguistic and rhetorical choices in texts.
Persuasive Communication is the closest scheduled advanced counterpart to public debate and argument.
Creative Communication Laboratory is the closest scheduled practice in producing public-facing creative work.
Communicating the Climate Crisis provides applied writing and communication for public audiences.
Introduction to Literary Studies supplies the closest scheduled disciplinary foundation, while UCR does not reproduce Dutch-language study.
Great Literary Works develops comparative literary interpretation relevant to literature in the contemporary world.
World Myth & Literature examines how narratives acquire cultural force across contexts.
Film & Text supplies advanced textual interpretation closest to the selected theory-and-stylistics choice.
Perspectives on Literary Meaning integrates advanced approaches to language, literature and interpretation.
Introduction to Film & Media examines mediated voices and stories in cultural context.
Media & the Environment is the closest scheduled counterpart to cultural narratives about landscape and ecology.
Writing Art's Histories develops sustained critical writing for specialist and public audiences.
History Research Seminar provides the closest scheduled independent humanities-research experience.
Introduction to Western Philosophy provides theoretical analysis adjacent to the selected language-and-theory pathway, while not reproducing Dutch linguistics.
Qualitative Research Methodology directly supplies qualitative social-research methods.
Ethics provides philosophical analysis relevant to language, literature and public reasoning.
Introduction to Sociology supplies social context for literacy and participation, without being literacy studies.
Statistics & Experimental Methods directly supplies quantitative research methods.
The 12-EC UvA space is genuinely open choice, so no fixed UCR course is asserted as its counterpart.

selection.assessment: Three feasible and materially distinct programmes are included: an integrated language-literature-communication closest match, a literature and cultural-history direction, and a public-language and society direction. They cover the evidence-backed directions at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: UvA provides an integrated Dutch-language disciplinary sequence spanning Dutch linguistics, literary history, writing and research. UCR offers substantial related study in literature, rhetoric, communication, media, cultural history and social research, but no Dutch linguistics, Dutch-language proficiency or Netherlands-specific literary-history sequence. The UCR alternatives therefore represent related academic directions rather than a full replacement for a Neerlandistiek degree.
